I've had a proper look, and yes — I accept it. This is the app we designed together.

I tried it for real, not just from the pictures. Pasting in a link I know, it went and pulled back the page's actual title, description, site name, icon, and picture on its own — exactly the "turn a bare link into something recognizable" behavior that started this whole thing. Saving it kept everything, including my note. When I tried to save the very same link again — even under a different title — it refused to make a second copy and pointed me back to the one I already had, which is just what I wanted. And deleting cleared it right out. The layout matches what we settled on, with my library, read-later, and archive shortcuts down the side and a search across everything up top.

You've also confirmed the two details I kept flagging — search that ignores capital letters, and labels that steer me toward the ones I already have so I don't make duplicates — are in there, along with all nineteen flows we worked through. The readable page-copy idea I raised is rightly set aside for the next round; I'm happy to leave it there.

It starts empty, ready for my first link, which is exactly how it should be. This is the bookmark home I wanted instead of the anonymous browser pile. I'm glad with it — let's complete this cycle.
